ownership_reason: Only the gold reads the bytes of the text and decides, per byte, whether it ends the data (the pad), adds six bits (a Base64 character) or is passed over: hops 1, 3 and 4 pass the text, the lookup table and the buffer along unchanged and hop 2 only sizes the buffer and trims the result to the octets written. The gold's javadoc promises to decode the Base64 characters found in an array of bytes; on the trigger's input ('{' and UTF-8 e-acute among Base64 characters) the gold indexes the lookup table with a code beyond it and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException inside itself, before any caller sees a result. The convention that bytes which are not Base64 characters are skipped whether or not they fall within the table's bounds, and never cause an exception, is pinned outside the gold: Base64.isBase64 tests 'octet >= 0 && octet < DECODE_TABLE.length' before the lookup and Base64Test testIsArrayByteBase64 rejects Byte.MIN_VALUE, -125, -10 and Byte.MAX_VALUE without an exception; the streaming decoder Base64.decode(byte[], int, int), used in production by Base64InputStream.read(byte[], int, int), makes the same bound test before its lookup and documents that it 'Ignores all non-base64 characters'; DECODE_TABLE's javadoc says only characters 'within the bounds of the array' are translated to -1; Base64Test testNonBase64Test ('RFC 2045 requires that all non base64 character be discarded, an exception should not have been thrown'), testIgnoringNonBase64InDecode and testCodec68 (CODEC-68, no ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException on non-Base64 bytes) pass.
